- Emit one diagnostic line containing counts only: settled tokens, margin, band, remaining hideable-entry count, and outcome. **Never include rendered ledger/message content.**
- Escalation metrics/cooldown across separate runs are follow-up work, not hidden state in v2.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Incident-shaped thin relief escalates.** With `force == false`, settled margins 14,503 / 14,990 / 21,000 at the 400k settings each cause exactly one checkpoint escalation. No hideable-exhaustion condition is required.
- **AC2 — Deep/healthy results are unchanged.** `margin >= settings.reserveTokens` performs no escalation, adds no pass record/log line, and preserves existing run results/reporting byte-for-byte where no other changed behavior is involved.
- **AC3 — Remaining hideables do not suppress escalation.** A thin result with one or more `_hideableEntries` remaining still escalates exactly once (regression against rejected v1).
- **AC4 — Exact boundaries.** `margin == 0` escalates; `0 < margin < reserveTokens` escalates; `margin == reserveTokens` and larger do not; `margin < 0` is not treated as a successful thin settlement and does not enter this success-side escalation path.
- **AC5 — Automatic-only gating.** Manual `force == true` and cap-forced runs do not escalate; ordinary automatic runs do. Existing gh-1742 invariant-1/factory behavior remains unchanged.
- **AC6 — Bounded work.** At most one escalation per `run()`; no hide-pass re-entry and no second escalation even when the pass leaves a thin margin. `maxCheckpointPasses == 0` produces no checkpoint call/append.
- **AC7 — Failure/no-work preserves verdict.** Empty range, empty summary, or append/processing failure leaves the pre-escalation under-trigger success standing and emits an explicit no-work/failed escalation report.
- **AC8 — Existing checkpoint safety holds.** Protected-tail ids, pins, pair integrity, keepRecent, depth-cap and expandable checkpoint coverage are preserved; marker-only ranges make no LLM call.
- **AC9 — Chunking and time budget are honest.** A test with multiple chunks proves they belong to one escalation pass; per-call `attemptBudget` applies to each call, while the factory `totalBudget` remains the overall bound. No new attempt starts after total-budget exhaustion.
- **AC10 — Cancellation is preserved.** Run/user cancellation during escalation follows existing cancellation semantics and is not swallowed into “optional escalation failed, success stands.”
- **AC11 — Observability is content-safe.** `checkpoint-escalation` reaches host reporting with margin/band/outcome; diagnostic output has counts only and no ledger content.
- **AC12 — Incident regression.** Replay-shaped tests for 385,619→360,497 and 375,609→360,010 now escalate on the same run. The next run starting under trigger performs no judge call and no escalation; no third judge-stall is required to obtain deeper relief.
- **AC13 — Existing suites remain green.** #148/#287/#387/#388/#515/#541/#729/#1379/#1409/#1425/#1742 regression suites pass; golden healthy-run reports do not drift.

## Test plan

### Unit

- `UT-ESC-1/2/3` — all three incident margins escalate; deep relief does not; hideables-remaining does not suppress escalation.
- `UT-ESC-4` — boundary table: negative, zero, `reserve−1`, `reserve`, `reserve+1` margins.
- `UT-ESC-5` — `force` and cap-forced matrix; no escalation on either forced channel.
- `UT-ESC-6` — exactly one pass; still-thin result does not loop; zero checkpoint-pass limit respected.
- `UT-ESC-7` — null range / empty summary / failed processing preserve verdict and report no-work/failure.
- `UT-ESC-8` — pins, protected tail, pair groups, keepRecent, depth cap and marker-only range.
- `UT-ESC-9` — cancellation is rethrown/propagated according to existing contracts.
- `UT-ESC-10` — pass kind/report/log metadata and content-safety.

### Integration

- `IT-ESC-1` — fake judge fails twice → deterministic hide lands at 360,497-equivalent → same run performs checkpoint escalation without requiring hides exhausted.
- `IT-ESC-2` — multi-chunk checkpoint: N summarizer calls, one escalation record; timeout on chunk K follows existing budget semantics and starts no chunk K+1.
- `IT-ESC-3` — host report contains the escalation kind and numeric reason; no rendered transcript in logs.
- `IT-ESC-4` — post-escalation under-trigger run performs no pre-flight work; repeated separate runs never share hidden escalation state.
- `IT-ESC-5` — provider-usage/rebuilt-estimate fixture: predicate and final verdict use the same `_requestTokens()` basis after refresh.

### Regression / merge rule

- `REG-ESC-1` — healthy deep-relief, ordinary forced, cap-forced and classic-fall-through goldens remain unchanged.
- `REG-ESC-2` — the two quoted incident transitions are merge-blocking fixtures; a fix that does not escalate both cannot merge even if generic escalation tests pass.
- Run the full compaction/auto-compactor suites, `dart analyze`, loc/CRAP/jscpd gates; cover all new branches (>90% target for new code, repository hard ratchet unchanged).

## Additional border cases

- Very small windows: band derives from scaled settings; no fixed 25k assumption and no escalation when the result is already at least one reserve below trigger.
- All foldable records pinned or protected: bounded no-op, no classic/lossy escape.
- Huge protected tail leaving little foldable prefix: no pair splitting or tail violation to manufacture relief.
- One checkpoint consumes several chunks on a slow smol endpoint: existing total budget remains authoritative; this card does not promise “one 300-second budget.”
- Escalation leaves tokens above trigger or still in the band: no second pass in that run; final verdict follows existing logic.
- Concurrent session/kill/resume during compaction: existing session and #1425 recovery behavior remains authoritative; no new resume protocol.

## Non-goals

- No change to deterministic-hide relief or #148 minimal-relief semantics.
- No judge payload cap, timeout retuning, circuit breaker, cross-run cooldown, or smol-role selection changes.
- No classic-engine escalation/fall-through from the structured engine.
- No change to trigger math, LRU re-hide, local-trim valve, manual `/compact`, message-cap forcing, or gh-1742 invariant 1.
- No new config keys, growth prediction, checkpoint quality rewrite, or changes to pins/protected-tail rules.

## Decisions after review (no open questions)

- **Band:** `margin < settings.reserveTokens`, strict `<`; half-reserve is rejected by incident data.
- **Second gate:** none. `hides exhausted` is diagnostic only; minimal hide cannot prove it.
- **Deepening mechanism:** existing structured checkpoint machinery only; no classic fallback in this card.
- **Scope:** automatic token-pressure runs only (`force == false`).
- **Metric/pass name:** `checkpoint-escalation`.
- **Time bound:** existing per-call attemptBudget plus factory totalBudget; one pass is not one LLM call.

## Follow-up (separate cards)

- Per-session hide-judge circuit breaker/cooldown after consecutive timeouts, so a known-dark endpoint is not retried twice on every later fire.
- #729-style bounded hide-judge input rather than full-ledger render.
- Optional factory-level classic fallback only if structured checkpoint machinery is unavailable, with its own failure/invariant contract.
- Escalation metrics and possible cross-run backoff based on shipped logs.

## References

- Code: `lib/src/compaction/structured/engine.dart` (`run`, `_runHidePasses`, `_runCheckpointPasses`, `_deterministicHide`, `_callJudge`, `_pickCheckpointRange`, `_chunkedFold`, `StructuredCompactionPass`); `lib/src/compaction/compaction.dart` (`CompactionSettings.forWindow`); `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart` (`AutoCompactorFactory.run`, `_runStructured`, total-budget and forced fall-through logic).
- Issues: #148 (hide-first/minimal relief), #1742 (scaled settings + invariant 1), #287/#387/#388 (structured engine/projection), #515/#540/#541/#740 (budgets and deterministic fallback), #729 (chunked payload budget), #1085 (over-window funnel), #1379/#1409 (LRU/pins), #1425 (local trim/recovery), #1636 (report UX), #1914 (detected-not-predicted precedent).
- Incident: `~/.fah/logs/fa.log`, sid `01a17c9c`, 2026-10-28/29; numeric table above is the acceptance oracle.

```text
band          = reserveTokens = 25,000
```

The v1 review exposed why `reserveTokens ~/ 2` was wrong. The shipped predicate must cover the actual incident:

| Settled tokens | `margin = trigger − tokensAfter` | `< reserveTokens` (v2) | `< reserveTokens ~/ 2` (rejected v1) |
|---:|---:|---|---|
| 360,497 | 14,503 | **escalate** | no |
| 360,010 | 14,990 | **escalate** | no |
| 354,000 | 21,000 | **escalate** | no |

Therefore v2 uses **strictly `margin < settings.reserveTokens`**, with no new configuration key.

## Verified mechanism (current code)

- **F1 — The pass loops stop at the trigger.** `lib/src/compaction/structured/engine.dart`: `_runHidePasses` returns when `before <= trigger` (:395); `_runCheckpointPasses` uses the same gate (:603). `run()` computes `trigger = window − settings.reserveTokens` and finally returns `_requestTokens() <= trigger`.
- **F2 — Settings scale with the window.** `CompactionSettings.forWindow` (`lib/src/compaction/compaction.dart` :463+) derives reserve/keepRecent from the window. At 400k: reserve 25,000, keepRecent 50,000. The band must derive from `settings.reserveTokens`, never a hard-coded incident constant.
- **F3 — Deterministic hide is intentionally minimal.** `_deterministicHide` stops when `freed >= over` (:516). It does **not** scan to exhaustion and does **not** prove that no hideable entries remain.
- **F4 — A thin result does not imply hides are exhausted.** After a successful fallback hide, `_runHidePasses` can return on under-trigger before evaluating remaining candidates. Consequently `hides exhausted` is not a valid required escalation gate; it is diagnostic state only.
- **F5 — The hide judge receives the full visible-ledger render.** `_callJudge` calls `judge(view.ledger.render())` under the per-attempt budget. Two consecutive failures select `_deterministicHide`. This explains the expensive degraded path, but changing judge payload/budget/circuit-breaking is outside this card.
- **F6 — Checkpoint passes are the structured deepening mechanism.** They consolidate the oldest projected prefix outside the keepRecent tail, hide included markers at marker cost, respect pins/protected-tail/pair integrity, and chunk payloads to the summarizer window (#729). One checkpoint pass may make several chunked summarizer calls.
- **F7 — Forced and automatic structured success differ at the factory.** `AutoCompactorFactory.run` returns structured success when `outcome.ok && adapter.passCount > 0`, including forced runs. Classic fall-through is not a generic “forced runs always deepen” mechanism. Escalation in this card therefore applies only when the engine was entered with `force == false`; manual force and message-cap-forced semantics stay unchanged.

## Retracted alternatives

- **Fatter deterministic hide:** rejected. It violates #148 minimal-relief semantics; deepening is a separate checkpoint pass.
- **Require `_hideableEntries(...).isEmpty`:** rejected. Minimal fallback does not establish exhaustion and this gate misses the target incident.
- **Half-reserve band:** rejected numerically; it misses every quoted incident result.
- **Predict future growth/re-crossing:** rejected. Evaluate the settled result directly, following the #1914 detected-not-predicted discipline.
- **Classic-engine fallback inside `StructuredCompactor`:** rejected layering. The structured engine does not own `AutoCompactorFactory.build()`; any factory-level classic fallback requires a separate contract/card.
- **Config-only remedy:** smol-role and judge-budget settings are operational mitigations, not a mechanism fix.

## Design

Add one post-ladder checkpoint escalation inside `StructuredCompactor.run`, before the final verdict:

```text
run(force)
 ├─ existing pre-flight / LRU re-hide / hide / checkpoint ladder — unchanged
 ├─ if force == false:
 │    tokensAfter = _requestTokens()             // same basis as verdict
 │    margin      = trigger − tokensAfter
 │    if 0 <= margin && margin < settings.reserveTokens:
 │       perform AT MOST ONE checkpoint escalation pass
 └─ return _requestTokens() <= trigger           // verdict rule unchanged
```

### Exact escalation semantics

1. **One pass, not one LLM call.** Select one checkpoint range and process it through the existing checkpoint machinery. A chunked range may require multiple summarizer calls; all are part of the same escalation pass.
2. **No hideable-entries precondition.** Thin settled headroom is sufficient evidence. Hideable entries may remain; escalation must still fire.
3. **Automatic runs only.** `force == true` skips escalation. Since message-cap forcing reaches the engine as `force: force || capTriggered`, cap-forced runs also retain their existing behavior. The normal automatic token-pressure path has `force == false`.
4. **Existing checkpoint limits remain authoritative.** `maxCheckpointPasses == 0` disables the escalation. Otherwise escalation adds exactly one pass beyond the ordinary ladder. It never re-enters hide passes and never loops because the result is still thin.
5. **No foldable range is a bounded no-op.** If `_pickCheckpointRange()` returns null (including an entirely pinned/exempt foldable prefix), emit one unsuccessful/no-work escalation report and keep the existing verdict; do not fall through to classic compaction.
6. **Failure safety.** If the pass cannot produce/append a checkpoint, the pre-escalation result is retained. A previously under-trigger success is not flipped to failure merely because optional deepening failed.
7. **Cancellation and budget expiry are not ordinary optional-pass failure.** User/run cancellation preserves cancellation. Factory total-budget timeout retains the existing #515/#1425 outcome path; escalation must not start another attempt after budget exhaustion or append additional late work after the authoritative timeout outcome.
8. **Projection invariants are inherited, not reimplemented.** Protected tail, pins, whole-pair groups, keepRecent, depth-cap flattening, marker consolidation and expandability behave exactly as in an ordinary checkpoint pass.
9. **Marker-only ranges remain deterministic.** Existing marker-consolidation behavior is reused; no fake LLM/judge call is reported and no repeated range loop is introduced.

### Observability

- Add pass kind **`checkpoint-escalation`** to `StructuredCompactionPass.kind` and surface it through existing `onPass` → host reporting (#1636).
- The pass/report identifies the triggering `marginTokens` and `bandTokens` (existing report models may carry these as optional metadata; no breaking change).
- Emit one diagnostic line containing counts only: settled tokens, margin, band, remaining hideable-entry count, and outcome. **Never include rendered ledger/message content.**
- Escalation metrics/cooldown across separate runs are follow-up work, not hidden state in v2.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Incident-shaped thin relief escalates.** With `force == false`, settled margins 14,503 / 14,990 / 21,000 at the 400k settings each cause exactly one checkpoint escalation. No hideable-exhaustion condition is required.
- **AC2 — Deep/healthy results are unchanged.** `margin >= settings.reserveTokens` performs no escalation, adds no pass record/log line, and preserves existing run results/reporting byte-for-byte where no other changed behavior is involved.
- **AC3 — Remaining hideables do not suppress escalation.** A thin result with one or more `_hideableEntries` remaining still escalates exactly once (regression against rejected v1).
- **AC4 — Exact boundaries.** `margin == 0` escalates; `0 < margin < reserveTokens` escalates; `margin == reserveTokens` and larger do not; `margin < 0` is not treated as a successful thin settlement and does not enter this success-side escalation path.
- **AC5 — Automatic-only gating.** Manual `force == true` and cap-forced runs do not escalate; ordinary automatic runs do. Existing gh-1742 invariant-1/factory behavior remains unchanged.
- **AC6 — Bounded work.** At most one escalation per `run()`; no hide-pass re-entry and no second escalation even when the pass leaves a thin margin. `maxCheckpointPasses == 0` produces no checkpoint call/append.
- **AC7 — Failure/no-work preserves verdict.** Empty range, empty summary, or append/processing failure leaves the pre-escalation under-trigger success standing and emits an explicit no-work/failed escalation report.
- **AC8 — Existing checkpoint safety holds.** Protected-tail ids, pins, pair integrity, keepRecent, depth-cap and expandable checkpoint coverage are preserved; marker-only ranges make no LLM call.
- **AC9 — Chunking and time budget are honest.** A test with multiple chunks proves they belong to one escalation pass; per-call `attemptBudget` applies to each call, while the factory `totalBudget` remains the overall bound. No new attempt starts after total-budget exhaustion.
- **AC10 — Cancellation is preserved.** Run/user cancellation during escalation follows existing cancellation semantics and is not swallowed into “optional escalation failed, success stands.”
- **AC11 — Observability is content-safe.** `checkpoint-escalation` reaches host reporting with margin/band/outcome; diagnostic output has counts only and no ledger content.
- **AC12 — Incident regression.** Replay-shaped tests for 385,619→360,497 and 375,609→360,010 now escalate on the same run. The next run starting under trigger performs no judge call and no escalation; no third judge-stall is required to obtain deeper relief.
- **AC13 — Existing suites remain green.** #148/#287/#387/#388/#515/#541/#729/#1379/#1409/#1425/#1742 regression suites pass; golden healthy-run reports do not drift.

## Test plan

### Unit

- `UT-ESC-1/2/3` — all three incident margins escalate; deep relief does not; hideables-remaining does not suppress escalation.
- `UT-ESC-4` — boundary table: negative, zero, `reserve−1`, `reserve`, `reserve+1` margins.
- `UT-ESC-5` — `force` and cap-forced matrix; no escalation on either forced channel.
- `UT-ESC-6` — exactly one pass; still-thin result does not loop; zero checkpoint-pass limit respected.
- `UT-ESC-7` — null range / empty summary / failed processing preserve verdict and report no-work/failure.
- `UT-ESC-8` — pins, protected tail, pair groups, keepRecent, depth cap and marker-only range.
- `UT-ESC-9` — cancellation is rethrown/propagated according to existing contracts.
- `UT-ESC-10` — pass kind/report/log metadata and content-safety.

### Integration

- `IT-ESC-1` — fake judge fails twice → deterministic hide lands at 360,497-equivalent → same run performs checkpoint escalation without requiring hides exhausted.
- `IT-ESC-2` — multi-chunk checkpoint: N summarizer calls, one escalation record; timeout on chunk K follows existing budget semantics and starts no chunk K+1.
- `IT-ESC-3` — host report contains the escalation kind and numeric reason; no rendered transcript in logs.
- `IT-ESC-4` — post-escalation under-trigger run performs no pre-flight work; repeated separate runs never share hidden escalation state.
- `IT-ESC-5` — provider-usage/rebuilt-estimate fixture: predicate and final verdict use the same `_requestTokens()` basis after refresh.

### Regression / merge rule

- `REG-ESC-1` — healthy deep-relief, ordinary forced, cap-forced and classic-fall-through goldens remain unchanged.
- `REG-ESC-2` — the two quoted incident transitions are merge-blocking fixtures; a fix that does not escalate both cannot merge even if generic escalation tests pass.
- Run the full compaction/auto-compactor suites, `dart analyze`, loc/CRAP/jscpd gates; cover all new branches (>90% target for new code, repository hard ratchet unchanged).

## Additional border cases

- Very small windows: band derives from scaled settings; no fixed 25k assumption and no escalation when the result is already at least one reserve below trigger.
- All foldable records pinned or protected: bounded no-op, no classic/lossy escape.
- Huge protected tail leaving little foldable prefix: no pair splitting or tail violation to manufacture relief.
- One checkpoint consumes several chunks on a slow smol endpoint: existing total budget remains authoritative; this card does not promise “one 300-second budget.”
- Escalation leaves tokens above trigger or still in the band: no second pass in that run; final verdict follows existing logic.
- Concurrent session/kill/resume during compaction: existing session and #1425 recovery behavior remains authoritative; no new resume protocol.

## Non-goals

- No change to deterministic-hide relief or #148 minimal-relief semantics.
- No judge payload cap, timeout retuning, circuit breaker, cross-run cooldown, or smol-role selection changes.
- No classic-engine escalation/fall-through from the structured engine.
- No change to trigger math, LRU re-hide, local-trim valve, manual `/compact`, message-cap forcing, or gh-1742 invariant 1.
- No new config keys, growth prediction, checkpoint quality rewrite, or changes to pins/protected-tail rules.

## Decisions after review (no open questions)

- **Band:** `margin < settings.reserveTokens`, strict `<`; half-reserve is rejected by incident data.
- **Second gate:** none. `hides exhausted` is diagnostic only; minimal hide cannot prove it.
- **Deepening mechanism:** existing structured checkpoint machinery only; no classic fallback in this card.
- **Scope:** automatic token-pressure runs only (`force == false`).
- **Metric/pass name:** `checkpoint-escalation`.
- **Time bound:** existing per-call attemptBudget plus factory totalBudget; one pass is not one LLM call.

## Follow-up (separate cards)

- Per-session hide-judge circuit breaker/cooldown after consecutive timeouts, so a known-dark endpoint is not retried twice on every later fire.
- #729-style bounded hide-judge input rather than full-ledger render.
- Optional factory-level classic fallback only if structured checkpoint machinery is unavailable, with its own failure/invariant contract.
- Escalation metrics and possible cross-run backoff based on shipped logs.

## References

- Code: `lib/src/compaction/structured/engine.dart` (`run`, `_runHidePasses`, `_runCheckpointPasses`, `_deterministicHide`, `_callJudge`, `_pickCheckpointRange`, `_chunkedFold`, `StructuredCompactionPass`); `lib/src/compaction/compaction.dart` (`CompactionSettings.forWindow`); `lib/src/agent/auto_compactor.dart` (`AutoCompactorFactory.run`, `_runStructured`, total-budget and forced fall-through logic).
- Issues: #148 (hide-first/minimal relief), #1742 (scaled settings + invariant 1), #287/#387/#388 (structured engine/projection), #515/#540/#541/#740 (budgets and deterministic fallback), #729 (chunked payload budget), #1085 (over-window funnel), #1379/#1409 (LRU/pins), #1425 (local trim/recovery), #1636 (report UX), #1914 (detected-not-predicted precedent).

## Hard architecture rules

- `lib/` is pure Dart: **no `dart:io`** (must compile for web). The only
  `dart:io` entry points are `bin/` and `lib/io.dart`; file/process/network
  behind tools goes through the `ExecutionEnv` abstraction.

## Working in parallel: shared checkout + worktrees

The user's primary working directory is this checkout — they may be
running an LLM loop here at the same time as any agent. To avoid
contention and stale-context confusion, agents follow this policy:

- **Do not modify files in this shared checkout unless the user asked for
  it.** For review, `gh api` + `git fetch` + `git show` /
  `git diff origin/<branch>..HEAD` is enough — no local checkout needed.
- **Do not run heavy commands in the shared checkout** (`dart test` for
  the whole suite, full `dart analyze`). They compete with the user's
  own LLM loop for CPU/IO and can flip its context mid-task.
- **Do not `git stash` the user's WIP.** Their uncommitted changes are
  sacred; never pop, drop, or apply them. If a checkout conflict blocks
  you, ask the user before touching `git stash`.
- **If a worktree is genuinely required** (running `dart test`/`analyze`
  locally against a non-current branch, exploring a fresh PR head):
  - **Ask the user first** whether to proceed — by default, review
    should not need a worktree at all.
  - If the user agrees, create under `flutter_agent/.worktrees/<name>/`
    (the in-repo location they picked — dot-prefix keeps it visually
    separate in `ls`, and `rm -rf .worktrees/` cleans everything in one
    shot). Never in the parent directory `../<name>/`, which has been
    the source of orphan pollution before.
  - Use `git worktree add --detach .worktrees/<name> origin/<branch>`
    against the remote tracking ref — never the local branch ref, which
    the user may have moved on.
  - **`git worktree remove` the moment you're done.** Don't leave stale
    worktrees behind.
  - The `.worktrees/` directory should be in `.gitignore` (so worktrees
    never get committed by accident). Add it there **only after
    confirming with the user** — silent `.gitignore` edits conflict
    with parallel agents who may already have it dirty.
- **Communicate with peer agents through the inbox fabric**, not by
  reading or writing their working files. `agent_directory` lists
  siblings; `agent_message` to the relevant mailbox id. Their
  `memory/note/` files are theirs — leave them alone.

## Memory is part of the system prompt

Before starting any non-trivial task, **search memory first** to pick up
durable facts the user has accumulated across sessions — preferences,
gotchas, conventions, prior decisions. Cheap to query, often the
difference between re-deriving a rule and silently violating it:

- `memory_search <topic>` for keyword search across both scopes
  (project = this repo, committed; user = global, private). Read the
  top results before acting.
- `memory_list` to skim recent entries when the topic is fuzzy or the
  user asks "what do you know about X".
- Project-scope notes under `memory/note/` are **the user's** — read
  freely, write only via `memory_add` (which goes through the package's
  policy: durable facts, supersede via delete+add, never leave solved
  problems to rot).
- User-scope notes are global across projects — facts about the user,
  their environment, their habits. Always relevant.

Common things memory already covers for this repo: worktree placement,
shared-checkout rules, agent messaging fabric, known fragile files,
prior false-blame incidents. If the task touches one of those, search
before you start.

## Golden tests are MANDATORY for UI work

Any change to `flutter_app/lib/` UI code is INCOMPLETE until its golden
tests are done right:

1. **Coverage first.** New widget file → tests in
   `test/golden/<area>_golden_test.dart` + map entry in
   `golden_guard_test.dart` (hard-fails otherwise). Changed visuals →
   regenerate affected snapshots.
2. **Real fonts.** `setUpAll(ensureGoldenFonts)` in every golden file;
   placeholder-box glyphs = garbage, redo.
3. **Full frames.** Snapshots are marketing material: full app frames
   (`goldenSizeDesktop` 1280x800, `goldenSizePhone` 390x844) with realistic
   content — never a widget floating on black void.
4. **Determinism.** Fixed data/timestamps, existing-test fakes, no
   network/engines/infinite animations.
5. **Eyes on pixels.** After `--update-goldens`, OPEN every changed PNG
   (no tofu, no overflow, legible buttons/icons) before committing.
6. **Green gate.** `flutter test test/golden` passes; pre-commit runs it +
   `scripts/check_goldens.py` (which also hard-fails on ORPHAN snapshots —
   committed PNGs no test references; delete stale files, never let them
   rot in git history).

## Prompts live outside Dart code

- Every LLM prompt is a Markdown file under `prompts/**` (example app:
  `flutter_app/prompts/`). Never prompt string literals in `.dart` files.
- Format: YAML frontmatter (`name`, `description`) between `---` lines,
  then body; runtime placeholders are `{{name}}` tokens.
- After editing a prompt: `dart run scripts/gen_prompts.dart` rewrites
  `lib/src/prompts/prompts.g.dart` + `flutter_app/lib/prompts.g.dart`
  (generated, never edit by hand); `test/prompts/prompts_sync_test.dart`
  gates drift.
- Bundled Codex model catalog
  (`lib/src/providers/chatgpt_codex_models_data.dart`) is generated from
  `codex-rs/models-manager/models.json` via
  `dart run scripts/sync_codex_models.dart`. Re-run the script when
  codex-rs ships a new catalog so the picker / OAuth default stay current
  without a manual edit.

## Quality gates (pre-commit hook: `scripts/pre-commit`)

The single CI gate is the SM pre-merge validation run (gh-1537): the
machine SM (#687, `machine-sm.yml` → factory-sm) updates the branch onto
main, dispatches `ci.yml` on the updated head, and merges only when green
— the tree that lands is byte-identical to the validated tree, so the
retired post-merge main CI run was pure repetition (and #1522's
tag-sourced versions remove the release-bot commits that retriggered it —
fewer main pushes → less SM queue churn). `ci.yml` fires on `v*` tags

For the escalation pass, the host-side diagnostic line would print automatically through the existing `onPass` rendering with `fallback=structured·ckpt-escalation tokens before→after ok=true`.

Since the adapter maps `StructuredCompactionPass` → `AutoCompactorPass`... adding margin/band to `AutoCompactorPass` would let the CLI print them. "settled tokens" = tokensAfter of the pre-escalation state... or the escalation report's tokensBefore. In the pass report: tokensBefore/tokensAfter cover settled tokens.

## Commits and releases

- Commit identity: human/AI contributors commit as `ai.teammate
  <agent.ai.native@gmail.com>` (history was rewritten to it — set
  `git config user.name ai.teammate` + `git config user.email
  agent.ai.native@gmail.com` repo-locally). Release TAGS from
  `scripts/auto_release.sh` are authored `fa-release-bot[bot]
  <fa-release-bot[bot]@users.noreply.github.com>` — the gh-1172 App pushes
  the annotated tag, so the App identity is what auditability hangs on.
  gh-1402 rule: ANY automation that commits/pushes release-path changes
  (store metadata fixes, release tags/releases) MUST use the fa-release-bot
  GitHub App token — never a PAT, never the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`
  (main's required status checks reject both, #1098).
- Commit subjects: `type(scope): ...` (`feat:`, `fix:`, `fix(example):`,
  `ci:`, `test(providers):`, `refactor(prompts):`).
- Every push to `main` cuts an annotated TAG (`scripts/auto_release.sh`
  via `ci.yml`) — ZERO commits land on main (gh-1522: the retired flow
  pushed a 4-file `chore(release):` bot commit per release). gh-1801: NO
  GitHub Release is created at tag-cut time (an asset-less create
  published an empty `latest` that broke `fa update`): the tag-run
  `binaries` job creates the release DRAFT-first via
  `scripts/release_lazy_draft.sh` (curated CHANGELOG notes via
  `release_notes.sh` + a `release-draft-owner` marker), every leg attaches
  into it, and `release-provenance` publishes + flags `latest` ONLY after
  the signed SHA256SUMS(.sig) is attached — `latest` never points at a
  release that cannot serve `fa update`. The git TAG is the single source
  of truth for versions:
  both pubspecs carry the FIXED `0.0.0-dev` placeholder (a hand-bump fails
  the Static `Version placeholder guard`), `pubspec.lock` never churns, and
  CI stamps the version at the edges: the `publish` job stamps the STAGED
  publish tree (pubspec version + generated changelog section prepend via
  `scripts/stamp_staged_release.sh`, staged version == tag guarded
  pre-upload), store/mobile builds stamp `--build-name/--build-number` from
  the derived tag version, `install_local.sh` stamps `version.txt` from
  `git describe`. CHANGELOG.md is curated-only: PRs add lines under
  `## Unreleased`; the release folds it into the tag's section AT STAGE
  TIME (`scripts/release_notes.sh` preference order: curated `## <version>`
  section → curated `## Unreleased` body → conventional commits since the
  previous tag). The version scheme is `1.0.<counter>` (gh-785: App Store
  Connect approved 1.0.0 and enforces a monotonic
  `CFBundleShortVersionString`, so the pre-promotion `0.1.<counter>`
  train can never upload again). Release checklist: push to main (or the
  `releaseDispatch` dispatch) → watch the ci.yml `release` job cut the tag
  → watch the tag-scoped `publish` + `binaries` + `release-provenance`
  jobs (the release publishes at the provenance step). `fa --version` reads
  the stamped `version.txt` first, the placeholder pubspec second.
- `packages/fa_llm` publishes per `fa_llm-v*` tag via
  `.github/workflows/publish-fa-llm.yml` (OIDC, no secrets). First
  publish of a NEW package is manual — pub.dev OIDC only uploads new
  versions of an existing package (issue #1511): owner runs
  `cd packages/fa_llm && dart pub publish` once, adds the OIDC publisher
  entry on pub.dev, then the workflow takes over. The workflow
  pre-flights the package-exists probe and exits 10 with the
  instructions on 404; see `packages/fa_llm/README.md` §Publishing.
- CLI binaries build per tag (`ci.yml` `binaries` job), attach to the
  GitHub Release (`fa-<os>-<arch>[.exe]`); `installer-smoke` verifies
  installers.
- App builds (`build-mobile.yml`, `build-macos.yml`, manual dispatch):
  Android AAB + iOS IPA on `[self-hosted, macOS, ARM64]`, macOS DMG/ZIP
  signed + notarized, TestFlight via `flutter_app/fastlane`. Optional
  secrets: `APP_STORE_CONNECT_KEY_ID/_ISSUER_ID/_KEY_CONTENT`,
  `MACOS_INSTALLER_P12_BASE64/_PASSWORD/MACOS_INSTALLER_CERT_ID`,
  `GOOGLE_SERVICE_INFO_PLIST_BASE64`. Both workflows hard-gate the binary
  on wasm_run FFI exports (`xcrun dyld_info -exports` must list
  `_wire_compile_wasm` — Podfiles force-load + `-exported_symbol` +
  `STRIP_STYLE=non-global`, else white screen on TestFlight). Pods cached
  keyed by `Podfile.lock`. The gate proves FFI exports ONLY — a Dart boot

# Changelog

Older entries: [CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md](CHANGELOG_ARCHIVE.md) — moved out
on 2026-10-09 (gh-1452): pub.dev server-rejects a publish whose
CHANGELOG.md exceeds its 262144-byte content cap, so this file keeps a
bounded recent window and `scripts/check_changelog_size.sh` fails fast when the cap is
approached. Since gh-1522 this file is CURATED-ONLY: add new lines under
`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
publish-staging time — the published artifact's changelog is generated
(and trimmed under the cap by `stamp_staged_release.sh`), and the
publish job only WARNS on this repo file, so this file's size can never
block a release again.

## Unreleased

- fix(gh-2003): the Copilot picker filter is tier-aware. Individual-tier
  `/models` responses omit `model_picker_enabled` entirely, so phase 1
  dropped every such entry as «picker flag absent» and individual/OAuth
  accounts still listed zero usable models. When the response comes from
  the individual tier — the individual host (`api.githubcopilot.com` or
  pi-mono's `api.individual.githubcopilot.com` spelling) or a
  no-proxy-ep token (individual by design) — an ABSENT flag is now
  selectable: absence ≠ an explicit `false`, which still drops
  everywhere (embeddings, completion-only). Business/enterprise answers
  keep the strict picker list unchanged, and the keep is never silent:
  the fetch note names it («2 of 2 models kept via the individual-tier
  fallback (picker flag absent)») through the existing `fetch notes:`
  surfacing. pi-mono parity: the trigger mirrors `allowPolicyFallback =
  baseUrl === "https://api.individual.githubcopilot.com"` in
  `packages/ai/src/auth/oauth/github-copilot.ts`.
- fix(gh-1990): the Copilot `/models` dialect never answers a silent
  empty list again. Every silent-empty exit names its branch through the
  new `fetchModelsForEndpointReport` dispatch (`ModelsFetchReport` +
  `ModelsFetchDiagnostic`): the token-exchange HTTP status (with the
  OAuth device-flow / fine-grained PAT remedies for classic `ghp_…`
  keys), the `/models` HTTP status or timeout (with the seat + per-tier
  host hint), proxy-ep-less individual tokens aimed at a business/
  enterprise configured host (the tier-misrouting hint), and the picker
  filter with per-model drop reasons (`picker flag absent`, `picker flag
  false`, `policy disabled`, `no tool_calls`, `endpoint unsupported`) —
8:`## Unreleased` and the release folds them into the tag's section at
14:## Unreleased

The wire marker text is the same `hiddenMarker(...)` shape as `hiddenMarkerTokens` — same seq source, same tokens, same preview. One difference: the wire marker for a hidden ToolResultMessage is a `ToolResultMessage` whose content is the marker TEXT; `estimateTokens(ToolResultMessage)` counts content chars — identical to `estimateTokens(UserMessage.text(same text))` (both count the text chars). So `hiddenMarkerTokens(record, seq)` == wire tokens exactly. 

Also assistant carriers: `_hiddenMessage` for AssistantMessage → probably a UserMessage marker — same shape ✓.

So Option F works exactly: settled = Σ_{visible} recordTokens + Σ_{hidden MessageRecords} hiddenMarkerTokens(record, seqOf(record.id)).

The seqOf: `RecordSeqIndex(await session.getEntries())` — let me double check RecordSeqIndex: it maps record.id → seq where seq = index+1 over ALL entries?? Let me check.

content.text:
# gh-2044: [GOAL] Auto-compact fragile-band escalation — one deepening pass when thin relief leaves hides exhausted

## Description

**[WIP][GOAL] Auto-compact fragile-band escalation — after any automatic structured run settles with less than one full reserve of headroom, perform exactly one bounded checkpoint deepening pass, whether or not hideable entries remain**

## Goal (v2 — review findings incorporated)

One sentence: **an automatic structured compaction that only just ducks under the trigger must not immediately re-enter the same expensive ladder — when its settled headroom is smaller than `settings.reserveTokens`, it performs exactly one additional structured checkpoint pass, while healthy/deep results and all forced-run semantics remain unchanged.**

This is a relief-quality fix, not a judge-timeout fix. The repeated 2×300 s judge stalls are a separate degraded-endpoint problem; this card reduces how quickly a thin result leads back to that ladder. A judge circuit breaker/cooldown is explicit follow-up work.

## Incident and numeric contract

Session sid `01a17c9c`, late Oct 2026, window 400,000 tokens (`contextWindow` override), smol role `glm-5.3-flash @ api.z.ai`.

`~/.fah/logs/fa.log` showed repeated hide-judge timeouts followed by deterministic hides:

```text
auto-compact start tokens=385619
auto-compact pass 2 FAILED — hide judge failed call / timeout (300 s)
hide-fallback tokens 385619→360497 ok=true
…next fire…
auto-compact pass 2 FAILED — hide judge failed call / timeout (300 s)
hide-fallback tokens 375609→360010 ok=true
…next fire…
auto-compact pass 1 local-trim tokens 360010→63268
```

A manual `/compact` subsequently cut approximately 354k→48k. Each automatic degraded fire could burn two judge attempts and still leave little headroom, so the next turn or two crossed the trigger again.

For a 400,000-token window, gh-1742 settings give:

```text
reserveTokens = 25,000
trigger       = 375,000
band          = reserveTokens = 25,000
```

The v1 review exposed why `reserveTokens ~/ 2` was wrong. The shipped predicate must cover the actual incident:

| Settled tokens | `margin = trigger − tokensAfter` | `< reserveTokens` (v2) | `< reserveTokens ~/ 2` (rejected v1) |
|---:|---:|---|---|
| 360,497 | 14,503 | **escalate** | no |
| 360,010 | 14,990 | **escalate** | no |
| 354,000 | 21,000 | **escalate** | no |

Therefore v2 uses **strictly `margin < settings.reserveTokens`**, with no new configuration key.

## Verified mechanism (current code)

- **F1 — The pass loops stop at the trigger.** `lib/src/compaction/structured/engine.dart`: `_runHidePasses` returns when `before <= trigger` (:395); `_runCheckpointPasses` uses the same gate (:603). `run()` computes `trigger = window − settings.reserveTokens` and finally returns `_requestTokens() <= trigger`.
- **F2 — Settings scale with the window.** `CompactionSettings.forWindow` (`lib/src/compaction/compaction.dart` :463+) derives reserve/keepRecent from the window. At 400k: reserve 25,000, keepRecent 50,000. The band must derive from `settings.reserveTokens`, never a hard-coded incident constant.
- **F3 — Deterministic hide is intentionally minimal.** `_deterministicHide` stops when `freed >= over` (:516). It does **not** scan to exhaustion and does **not** prove that no hideable entries remain.
- **F4 — A thin result does not imply hides are exhausted.** After a successful fallback hide, `_runHidePasses` can return on under-trigger before evaluating remaining candidates. Consequently `hides exhausted` is not a valid required escalation gate; it is diagnostic state only.
- **F5 — The hide judge receives the full visible-ledger render.** `_callJudge` calls `judge(view.ledger.render())` under the per-attempt budget. Two consecutive failures select `_deterministicHide`. This explains the expensive degraded path, but changing judge payload/budget/circuit-breaking is outside this card.
- **F6 — Checkpoint passes are the structured deepening mechanism.** They consolidate the oldest projected prefix outside the keepRecent tail, hide included markers at marker cost, respect pins/protected-tail/pair integrity, and chunk payloads to the summarizer window (#729). One checkpoint pass may make several chunked summarizer calls.
- **F7 — Forced and automatic structured success differ at the factory.** `AutoCompactorFactory.run` returns structured success when `outcome.ok && adapter.passCount > 0`, including forced runs. Classic fall-through is not a generic “forced runs always deepen” mechanism. Escalation in this card therefore applies only when the engine was entered with `force == false`; manual force and message-cap-forced semantics stay unchanged.

## Retracted alternatives

- **Fatter deterministic hide:** rejected. It violates #148 minimal-relief semantics; deepening is a separate checkpoint pass.
- **Require `_hideableEntries(...).isEmpty`:** rejected. Minimal fallback does not establish exhaustion and this gate misses the target incident.
- **Half-reserve band:** rejected numerically; it misses every quoted incident result.
- **Predict future growth/re-crossing:** rejected. Evaluate the settled result directly, following the #1914 detected-not-predicted discipline.
- **Classic-engine fallback inside `StructuredCompactor`:** rejected layering. The structured engine does not own `AutoCompactorFactory.build()`; any factory-level classic fallback requires a separate contract/card.
- **Config-only remedy:** smol-role and judge-budget settings are operational mitigations, not a mechanism fix.

## Design

Add one post-ladder checkpoint escalation inside `StructuredCompactor.run`, before the final verdict:

```text
run(force)
 ├─ existing pre-flight / LRU re-hide / hide / checkpoint ladder — unchanged
 ├─ if force == false:
 │    tokensAfter = _requestTokens()             // same basis as verdict
 │    margin      = trigger − tokensAfter
 │    if 0 <= margin && margin < settings.reserveTokens:
 │       perform AT MOST ONE checkpoint escalation pass
 └─ return _requestTokens() <= trigger           // verdict rule unchanged
```

### Exact escalation semantics

1. **One pass, not one LLM call.** Select one checkpoint range and process it through the existing checkpoint machinery. A chunked range may require multiple summarizer calls; all are part of the same escalation pass.
2. **No hideable-entries precondition.** Thin settled headroom is sufficient evidence. Hideable entries may remain; escalation must still fire.
3. **Automatic runs only.** `force == true` skips escalation. Since message-cap forcing reaches the engine as `force: force || capTriggered`, cap-forced runs also retain their existing behavior. The normal automatic token-pressure path has `force == false`.
4. **Existing checkpoint limits remain authoritative.** `maxCheckpointPasses == 0` disables the escalation. Otherwise escalation adds exactly one pass beyond the ordinary ladder. It never re-enters hide passes and never loops because the result is still thin.
5. **No foldable range is a bounded no-op.** If `_pickCheckpointRange()` returns null (including an entirely pinned/exempt foldable prefix), emit one unsuccessful/no-work escalation report and keep the existing verdict; do not fall through to classic compaction.
6. **Failure safety.** If the pass cannot produce/append a checkpoint, the pre-escalation result is retained. A previously under-trigger success is not flipped to failure merely because optional deepening failed.
7. **Cancellation and budget expiry are not ordinary optional-pass failure.** User/run cancellation preserves cancellation. Factory total-budget timeout retains the existing #515/#1425 outcome path; escalation must not start another attempt after budget exhaustion or append additional late work after the authoritative timeout outcome.
8. **Projection invariants are inherited, not reimplemented.** Protected tail, pins, whole-pair groups, keepRecent, depth-cap flattening, marker consolidation and expandability behave exactly as in an ordinary checkpoint pass.
9. **Marker-only ranges remain deterministic.** Existing marker-consolidation behavior is reused; no fake LLM/judge call is reported and no repeated range loop is introduced.

### Observability

- Add pass kind **`checkpoint-escalation`** to `StructuredCompactionPass.kind` and surface it through existing `onPass` → host reporting (#1636).
- The pass/report identifies the triggering `marginTokens` and `bandTokens` (existing report models may carry these as optional metadata; no breaking change).
- Emit one diagnostic line containing counts only: settled tokens, margin, band, remaining hideable-entry count, and outcome. **Never include rendered ledger/message content.**
- Escalation metrics/cooldown across separate runs are follow-up work, not hidden state in v2.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC1 — Incident-shaped thin relief escalates.** With `force == false`, settled margins 14,503 / 14,990 / 21,000 at the 400k settings each cause exactly one checkpoint escalation. No hideable-exhaustion condition is required.
- **AC2 — Deep/healthy results are unchanged.** `margin >= settings.reserveTokens` performs no escalation, adds no pass record/log line, and preserves existing run results/reporting byte-for-byte where no other changed behavior is involved.
- **AC3 — Remaining hideables do not suppress escalation.** A thin result with one or more `_hideableEntries` remaining still escalates exactly once (regression against rejected v1).
- **AC4 — Exact boundaries.** `margin == 0` escalates; `0 < margin < reserveTokens` escalates; `margin == reserveTokens` and larger do not; `margin < 0` is not treated as a successful thin settlement and does not enter this success-side escalation path.
- **AC5 — Automatic-only gating.** Manual `force == true` and cap-forced runs do not escalate; ordinary automatic runs do. Existing gh-1742 invariant-1/factory behavior remains unchanged.
- **AC6 — Bounded work.** At most one escalation per `run()`; no hide-pass re-entry and no second escalation even when the pass leaves a thin margin. `maxCheckpointPasses == 0` produces no checkpoint call/append.
- **AC7 — Failure/no-work preserves verdict.** Empty range, empty summary, or append/processing failure leaves the pre-escalation under-trigger success standing and emits an explicit no-work/failed escalation report.
- **AC8 — Existing checkpoint safety holds.** Protected-tail ids, pins, pair integrity, keepRecent, depth-cap and expandable checkpoint coverage are preserved; marker-only ranges make no LLM call.
- **AC9 — Chunking and time budget are honest.** A test with multiple chunks proves they belong to one escalation pass; per-call `attemptBudget` applies to each call, while the factory `totalBudget` remains the overall bound. No new attempt starts after total-budget exhaustion.
- **AC10 — Cancellation is preserved.** Run/user cancellation during escalation follows existing cancellation semantics and is not swallowed into “optional escalation failed, success stands.”
- **AC11 — Observability is content-safe.** `checkpoint-escalation` reaches host reporting with margin/band/outcome; diagnostic output has counts only and no ledger content.
- **AC12 — Incident regression.** Replay-shaped tests for 385,619→360,497 and 375,609→360,010 now escalate on the same run. The next run starting under trigger performs no judge call and no escalation; no third judge-stall is required to obtain deeper relief.
- **AC13 — Existing suites remain green.** #148/#287/#387/#388/#515/#541/#729/#1379/#1409/#1425/#1742 regression suites pass; golden healthy-run reports do not drift.

## Test plan

### Unit

- `UT-ESC-1/2/3` — all three incident margins escalate; deep relief does not; hideables-remaining does not suppress escalation.
- `UT-ESC-4` — boundary table: negative, zero, `reserve−1`, `reserve`, `reserve+1` margins.
- `UT-ESC-5` — `force` and cap-forced matrix; no escalation on either forced channel.
- `UT-ESC-6` — exactly one pass; still-thin result does not loop; zero checkpoint-pass limit respected.
- `UT-ESC-7` — null range / empty summary / failed processing preserve verdict and report no-work/failure.
- `UT-ESC-8` — pins, protected tail, pair groups, keepRecent, depth cap and marker-only range.
- `UT-ESC-9` — cancellation is rethrown/propagated according to existing contracts.
- `UT-ESC-10` — pass kind/report/log metadata and content-safety.

### Integration

- `IT-ESC-1` — fake judge fails twice → deterministic hide lands at 360,497-equivalent → same run performs checkpoint escalation without requiring hides exhausted.
- `IT-ESC-2` — multi-chunk checkpoint: N summarizer calls, one escalation record; timeout on chunk K follows existing budget semantics and starts no chunk K+1.
- `IT-ESC-3` — host report contains the escalation kind and numeric reason; no rendered transcript in logs.
- `IT-ESC-4` — post-escalation under-trigger run performs no pre-flight work; repeated separate runs never share hidden escalation state.
- `IT-ESC-5` — provider-usage/rebuilt-estimate fixture: predicate and final verdict use the same `_requestTokens()` basis after refresh.

### Regression / merge rule

- `REG-ESC-1` — healthy deep-relief, ordinary forced, cap-forced and classic-fall-through goldens remain unchanged.
- `REG-ESC-2` — the two quoted incident transitions are merge-blocking fixtures; a fix that does not escalate both cannot merge even if generic escalation tests pass.
- Run the full compaction/auto-compactor suites, `dart analyze`, loc/CRAP/jscpd gates; cover all new branches (>90% target for new code, repository hard ratchet unchanged).

## Additional border cases

- Very small windows: band derives from scaled settings; no fixed 25k assumption and no escalation when the result is already at least one reserve below trigger.
- All foldable records pinned or protected: bounded no-op, no classic/lossy escape.
- Huge protected tail leaving little foldable prefix: no pair splitting or tail violation to manufacture relief.
- One checkpoint consumes several chunks on a slow smol endpoint: existing total budget remains authoritative; this card does not promise “one 300-second budget.”
- Escalation leaves tokens above trigger or still in the band: no second pass in that run; final verdict follows existing logic.
- Concurrent session/kill/resume during compaction: existing session and #1425 recovery behavior remains authoritative; no new resume protocol.

## Non-goals

- No change to deterministic-hide relief or #148 minimal-relief semantics.
- No judge payload cap, timeout retuning, circuit breaker, cross-run cooldown, or smol-role selection changes.
- No classic-engine escalation/fall-through from the structured engine.
- No change to trigger math, LRU re-hide, local-trim valve, manual `/compact`, message-cap forcing, or gh-1742 invariant 1.
- No new config keys, growth prediction, checkpoint quality rewrite, or changes to pins/protected-tail rules.

## Decisions after review (no open questions)

- **Band:** `margin < settings.reserveTokens`, strict `<`; half-reserve is rejected by incident data.
- **Second gate:** none. `hides exhausted` is diagnostic only; minimal hide cannot prove it.
- **Deepening mechanism:** existing structured checkpoint machinery only; no classic fallback in this card.
- **Scope:** automatic token-pressure runs only (`force == false`).
- **Metric/pass name:** `checkpoint-escalation`.
- **Time bound:** existing per-call attemptBudget plus factory totalBudget; one pass is not one LLM call.

## Follow-up (separate cards)

- Per-session hide-judge circuit breaker/cooldown after consecutive timeouts, so a known-dark endpoint is not retried twice on every later fire.
- #729-style bounded hide-judge input rather than full-ledger render.
- Optional factory-level classic fallback only if structured checkpoint machinery is unavailable, with its own failure/invariant contract.
- Escalation metrics and possible cross-run backoff based on shipped logs.

arguments.content:
### What changed
Added the fragile-band escalation to `StructuredCompactor.run`: an automatic structured compaction (`force == false`) that settles with `0 <= trigger - settled < settings.reserveTokens` headroom now performs exactly one extra checkpoint pass through the existing checkpoint machinery, instead of leaving the next turn to re-enter the full judge ladder (incident sid `01a17c9c`).

### Key decisions
- Band is `settings.reserveTokens`, strict `<` — the rejected half-reserve v1 misses every quoted incident margin (14,503 / 14,990 / 21,000 at the 400k window).
- Thin settled headroom is the only gate: no hideable-exhaustion precondition (the minimal fallback cannot prove exhaustion); the remaining-hideable count rides the report as a diagnostic only.
- Forced runs (manual `/compact` and the message-cap channel) and `maxCheckpointPasses == 0` keep their existing behavior; at most one escalation per `run()`, never a hide re-entry, never a loop.
- Projection invariants are inherited, not reimplemented: pins, protected tail, whole-pair groups, keepRecent, depth cap, marker-only deterministic consolidation (no LLM call), and the #729 chunked fold.
- Cancellation surfaces (run aborted → failure, not "optional pass failed"); a total-budget expiry stays the factory's authoritative #515 outcome — no append or report after it.
- Observability: new `checkpoint-escalation` pass kind with `marginTokens`/`bandTokens`/`hideableRemaining` metadata on `StructuredCompactionPass` and `AutoCompactorPass`; the CLI diagnostic line gains counts-only fields (`margin= band= hideable-left=`) and stays byte-identical on every other pass.

### How to verify
```bash
dart test test/compaction/structured_escalation_test.dart   # 22 new tests (UT/IT-ESC-1..11)
dart test test/compaction/                                   # full compaction suites stay green
```
Incident-shaped regressions (REG-ESC-2): 385,619→360,497 and 375,609→360,010 replays escalate on the same run; a next run starting under the trigger performs no judge call and no escalation.
